_comment: spec docs/spec/2026-09-03-FollowTestSuite.md §3.6/§4.15. Single source of truth for FollowManager::applyConfig() (C++), mock_server.py's validate_config() (Python), and html/follow-logic.js's validateConfig() (JS). `overrides` is applied on top of `baseline` below. cppValid/pythonValid/jsValid are independent per-validator expectations -- NOT one shared expectValid -- because tracing all three (while drafting this fixture) found the three validators don't actually implement the same rule set: §2.3's original 'Python mirrors only the C++ rules, JS is a strict superset' characterization undersells it. See each case's `note` for the specific divergence; summarized in docs/spec/2026-09-03-FollowTestSuite.md §7.

cases.name: emitHz_zero_fails
cases.note: shared rule -- all three implement this identically

cases.name: geometry_insane_fails_cpp_and_js_only
cases.note: FINDING: mock_server.py's validate_config() has no offsetGeometrySane() equivalent at all -- it never checks ofsLongM/ofsLatM/ofsVertM against minSepM/minVSepM, so a geometrically-insane config passes Python validation. Not in spec's original §2.3 analysis.

cases.name: target_peer_out_of_range_fails_cpp_only
cases.note: FINDING: neither mock_server.py nor follow.js check targetPeer against NODES_MAX -- only FollowManager::applyConfig() does. Not in spec's original §2.3 analysis.

cases.name: status_gvar_index_out_of_range_fails_cpp_and_python_only
cases.note: FINDING: follow.js's validateConfig() never range-checks any GVAR index field (-1 or 0-7) -- it only checks GVAR-index *uniqueness* (see gvar_indices_not_unique_fails below), not individual validity. C++ and Python both enforce the range.

cases.name: rc_long_channel_out_of_range_fails_cpp_and_python_only
cases.note: FINDING: follow.js never range-checks RC channel fields (-1 or 1-16) -- only channel *uniqueness* (see rc_channels_not_unique_fails below). C++ and Python both enforce the range.

cases.name: max_target_speed_not_greater_than_min_fails_cpp_and_python_only
cases.note: FINDING: follow.js never checks maxTargetSpeedMps > minTargetSpeedMps >= 0 at all (only the autothrottle arm-switch threshold ordering, a different field pair -- see autothrottle_threshold_order_fails below).

cases.name: gvar_indices_not_unique_fails_js_only
cases.note: JS-only superset rule (spec §2.3, documented finding §7.1): a raw POST bypassing the UI can set overlapping GVAR indices and the firmware accepts it.

cases.name: autothrottle_threshold_order_fails_js_only
cases.note: JS-only superset rule, deliberately not duplicated server-side per mock_server.py's own comment (spec §2.3).
